name: Broadsheet — WordPress + Spacefast Zero
title: WordPress + Zero
summary: A magazine whose articles come from a public WordPress REST API at build time and render to static pages, with a Spacefast Zero server behind them for realtime emoji reactions and server-side search over a build-time index.
setup_questions: Which WordPress site should the articles come from (any public site URL or /wp-json REST root, e.g. https://wordpress.org/news)?
What should the publication be called?
What's the accent color (a hex like #d9410b)?
sections: Masthead with the publication name, a server-backed search box, and the WordPress source credited
Magazine index: a full-bleed lead story plus a responsive grid of article cards (featured image, categories, title, excerpt, author, date, reading time)
Static article pages rendering the post's own WordPress HTML as editorial prose — images, embeds, blockquotes, tables, and code blocks all handled
A realtime emoji reaction bar on every article, backed by the Zero database and live across browsers
Search results served by GET /api/search from an index compiled into the capsule at build time
Colophon explaining which half of the page is static and which half is the runtime
based_on: The setup a real team lands on when WordPress is the editor but the site should be static: content pulled through the @spacefast/wordpress client at build time, rendered to flat HTML, with one Spacefast Zero capsule adding the few things a static file cannot do.
why_good: The flagship composition example — build-time headless WordPress and a request-time Zero server in the same space, one sf.jsonc, one publish. It is the only recipe where static rendering and a live database sit on the same page.
notes: Run and publish from site/. Zero runtime project, not a prebuilt static directory. `bun run build` must run before `sf build`: it fetches WordPress, generates shared/search-index.ts for the capsule, and renders home.html plus posts/*.html into the capsule root. Those generated files are gitignored. Publish with `sf publish --skip-build` (or `bun run publish`) — a Zero project with a `build` script otherwise sends sf publish down the static-site path and it fails looking for a dist/. sf dev previews the Zero server and client only; the static tree is exercised on a published space.
